{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfdwQXuYgKVLmJi2XP3Xj","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky factorization in `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` now always runs on the GPU with CUDA. Its results match the original sequential version, and on one RTX 3090 it runs at about the card's FP64 peak for large matrices. I only changed `cholesky.cpp` and `CMakeLists.txt`, and the executable is still `cholesky`.\n\n**How it works**\n- **Factorization:** the matrix is split into 64×64 blocks and processed block by block. For each one, the GPU factors the diagonal block, solves the column of blocks below it, and then updates the rest of the lower triangle. That last update is almost all the work, and it runs as a tiled double-precision matrix-multiply kernel.\n- **Overlap:** while the rest of the matrix is being updated, the next block column is already updated and factored on a second stream. Each finished block of rows is copied back to the host on a third stream while computation continues. The host buffer is pinned (locked in memory) before the timer starts, so these copies can overlap.\n- **Same behaviour as before:** a non-positive-definite matrix is still detected with the same `val <= 0.0` test. Later GPU work stops and the same error message is printed with the first failing index. The upper triangle is still zeroed and the result ends up in `A` on the host.\n- **Generation and validation:** both `B·Bᵀ + n·I` and the validation product `L·Lᵀ` now run on the GPU with the same multiply kernel. The random numbers still come from the sequential `rand_r` loop, so the input matrix is the same as before.\n- **Timing:** the timed region includes the copy to the GPU, the factorization and the copy back.\n- **CMake:** it now enables the CUDA language, compiles `cholesky.cpp` as CUDA, targets the native GPU architecture, defaults to a Release build and links `CUDA::cudart`. There are no new external dependencies.\n\n**Checks**\n- For n = 100, 512, 1000 and 2048, the output statistics (sum, min, max) match the original program to the last 1–2 digits. The exact hash will differ because the additions happen in a different order.\n- Validation (`-v`) passes for n = 1, 2, 63, 64, 65, 129, 1023 and 3001 (sizes that don't divide evenly into 64×64 blocks). The relative error is at most about 2e-9, against a tolerance of 1e-6.\n- I did not test the non-positive-definite error path, because the generator always produces a valid matrix. I checked that code by reading it only.\n\n**Performance**\n\n| n | Original (CPU) | CUDA |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 29 ms | 3 ms |\n| 2048 | 2131 ms | 19 ms |\n| 4096 | — | 65 ms (352 GFLOPS) |\n| 8192 | — | 376 ms (487 GFLOPS) |\n| 16384 | — | 2642 ms (555 GFLOPS) |\n\nThe code uses one GPU. Going faster would mean splitting the work across the machine's 4 GPUs, which would make the code a lot more complex; I can do that if you want it."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":429,"cache_read_input_tokens":36893,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":429},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"48fb4039-1f44-4f93-bba2-ddeb8e1934ea","uuid":"a6a0452c-7e08-448c-88a3-471df1664e18","timestamp":"2026-10-02T19:10:27.012Z","request_id":"req_011CfdwQXRGxR4Ho716QDqJJ"}
